overview: Core Lithium is an ASX-listed developer/producer of hard-rock spodumene lithium concentrate, 100% owner of the Finniss Lithium Operation 88km by road from the Port of Darwin in Australia's Northern Territory. Finniss produced first concentrate in early 2023 but mining and processing were suspended in 2024 amid a lithium price crash; after an 18-month care-and-maintenance period and a fully funded restart package backed by Glencore, InfraVia Capital Partners and Nebari, the Board approved a Final Investment Decision in March 2026 and mining resumed at the Grants open pit, with first new-production spodumene shipment targeted for the December quarter of CY2026 and underground development at BP33 underway toward a 2028 steady state of 1.2Mtpa. The company also holds exploration assets (Blackbeard lithium prospect, Shoobridge gold) and recently divested non-core uranium tenements.

business_model.summary: Single-asset hard-rock lithium miner. Revenue comes from selling spodumene (lithium) concentrate and lithium 'fines' (a lower-grade by-product) to offtake/trading partners, priced off benchmark spodumene indices (e.g. Fastmarkets SC6 CIF China) with quotation-period true-up adjustments. Operations were suspended for roughly two years (2024-2026); during that period the company had zero or negative revenue (price adjustments on legacy sales only) and funded itself from cash reserves, equity raises and new debt/convertible notes. Revenue only resumed in FY2026 (~A$17.8m, mostly one-off stockpile sales of accumulated spodumene concentrate and lithium fines) ahead of the restart of continuous mined production.

revenue_streams.name: Spodumene concentrate sales (new production, restarting)
revenue_streams.trend: restarting - first shipment targeted December quarter CY2026

revenue_streams.name: Stockpile sales (spodumene concentrate + lithium fines, one-off)
revenue_streams.trend: one-off / depleting - ~A$38.5m realized to date across FY26 and early FY27, remaining stockpile largely sold

revenue_streams.name: Royalty on third-party uranium production (Napperby, 1% NSR)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - concentrate sold to global trading/offtake partners (five-year marketing agreement with Glencore covering all future spodumene concentrate; prior offtake agreements with Yahua and Tesla/Ganfeng were terminated/settled during the suspension)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Northern Territory, Australia asset; product exported via Darwin Port, predominantly to Asian (China-linked) lithium chemical converters

main_competitors: Mineral Resources (MIN.AX) / Albemarle JVs (Wodgina, Mt Marion)
competitive_position.market_position: Small-cap, sub-scale Australian hard-rock lithium producer re-entering the market; materially smaller by volume than Pilbara Minerals or Greenbushes, and higher on the industry cost curve than the largest incumbents

moat_factors.description: Only 88km by sealed road from Darwin Port, Australia's closest major port to Asian lithium converters, giving a freight-cost and shipping-time advantage versus WA Pilbara-based peers

Over A$250m already invested in a DMS processing plant, mining fleet readiness and site infrastructure; 100% ownership of the crushing circuit (acquired FY25) halves crushing costs and removes a prior third-party contract
15.6Mt Ore Reserve (Grants, BP33, Carlton) supporting an estimated 20-year mine life and 214ktpa nameplate spodumene concentrate at steady state, with exploration upside at Blackbeard
Glencore (marketing + convertible note), InfraVia and Nebari provide funding certainty, offtake credibility and access to global sales channels not typically available to a junior of this size

weaknesses: Single-asset, single-commodity producer with no production diversification
High-cost, sub-scale relative to tier-1 Australian and South American lithium producers; historically needed a lithium-price recovery and a cost-reduction redesign (Restart Study) just to restart
Recently emerged from a ~2-year suspension - restart execution risk is unproven (ramp-up, plant optimisation, underground development at BP33 all still in progress)

Heavy reliance on external financing (equity raises, convertible notes, senior secured debt) rather than self-funded cash flow, with extensive shareholder dilution over time (shares outstanding grew from ~272m in FY2016 to ~3.24bn by FY2026)
Thin/negative margins highly sensitive to spot spodumene prices, which remain volatile and depressed versus 2022-2023 peaks

growth_drivers: Ramp-up of Grants open pit mining and processing to first new concentrate shipment (targeted December quarter CY2026)
BP33 underground mine development (A$274m contract with Develop Global) targeting first ore mid-CY2027 and contributing to 1.2Mtpa steady-state production by mid-CY2028
Updated, larger Ore Reserve at Grants and Carlton (33% increase in tonnage, 44% increase in contained metal) extending mine life and improving project economics
Blackbeard exploration target (7-10Mt lithium) and newly acquired Bynoe tenement from Charger Metals, offering resource growth beyond current 1.2Mtpa plant capacity
Five-year Glencore marketing agreement giving access to global sales channels while retaining flexibility for direct offtake/spot sales
Potential cyclical recovery in spodumene/lithium prices as EV adoption, grid storage and electrification demand growth outpaces new supply (bullish broker and bank forecasts, though contested)
Non-core asset monetisation (uranium tenements sold to Elevate Uranium for cash + royalty; gold exploration assets spun out into Axiant Resources) sharpening focus and strengthening the balance sheet

business.description: All value is tied to Finniss; any technical, geotechnical, weather (NT wet season) or permitting setback directly impairs the whole company

Finniss only recommenced mining in 2026 after ~2 years of care and maintenance; commissioning/optimisation of the plant, ramp-up to nameplate throughput, and the BP33 underground build are all unproven in the current cost structure
Revenue and project economics are directly tied to volatile spodumene/lithium prices, which fell ~80% from 2022 peaks and precipitated the original 2024 suspension
Reliance on NRW (Grants mining contract) and Develop Global (BP33 underground contract) for on-schedule, on-budget delivery of restart milestones

financial.description: Restart funded partly by US$120m of debt/convertible notes (Glencore, InfraVia, Nebari) alongside equity, introducing debt service and potential conversion dilution that the company did not carry historically
Shares outstanding have grown roughly 12x since 2016 (to ~3.2bn by FY2026) via repeated capital raises (including A$120m and A$50m placements in FY2026) to fund losses and the restart
Company posted net losses in every year from FY2016-FY2026 even while producing; renewed near-term losses are likely until Grants/BP33 reach steady-state cash flow

regulatory.description: Historical dispute with the Northern Territory Revenue Office over FY23 mineral royalty assessment (~A$6.4m), now under a negotiated instalment repayment plan

Legislative changes required incorporation of revised water extraction licences into Mining Management Plans for Grants and BP33; ongoing wet-season water management and discharge compliance obligations
Operations require ongoing engagement with Northern Territory Government and traditional owners as part of social licence to operate

macro.description: Forecasters (e.g. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence) see the current supply glut persisting or deepening through 2027 as idled Australian and Chinese (lepidolite) capacity restarts, which could depress prices just as Core ramps back up
Chinese EV and battery demand, converter margins and consumption-tax policy heavily influence spodumene pricing, Core's primary end-market

Spodumene is typically priced in USD while costs are predominantly AUD-denominated, creating FX translation effects on margins; diesel/fuel and contractor labour cost inflation also affect NT mining costs

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Highly bifurcated views: bearish commentary (Benchmark Mineral Intelligence and others) expects the lithium supply glut to persist or deepen through 2027 as idled capacity (including Chinese lepidolite and other Australian spodumene mines) returns; bullish views (e.g. UBS) point to a structural deficit emerging through 2026-H1 2027 on EV, grid-storage and electrification demand outpacing new supply, with spot prices recovering sharply off 2025 lows (roughly US$8,000/t to US$20,000+/t range cited through 2026). Outcomes for Core are highly sensitive to which scenario plays out.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Highly cyclical - lithium is a boom/bust commodity; Core itself is a case study, having built, operated, suspended, and restarted the same asset within a single commodity cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - new debt/convertible note funding package increases sensitivity to interest costs and refinancing conditions versus the company's prior debt-free structure
key_input_costs: Diesel/fuel for mining fleet and haulage
Mining and underground development contractor costs (NRW, Develop Global)
Freight and shipping via Darwin Port

recent_developments.event: Release of Restart Study repositioning Finniss as a lower-cost, long-life operation: ~40% lower mining costs, ~33% lower processing costs, 29% lower pre-production capex, throughput increased to 1.2Mtpa
A$50m equity raising (Placement + Share Purchase Plan at $0.105/share) to accelerate FID readiness
Settlement/termination of Ganfeng offtake agreement (US$2.0m payment) and binding settlement discontinuing Tesla offtake discussions, unencumbering future Finniss production
Updated Grants and Carlton Ore Reserves (33% tonnage increase at Grants); two binding stockpile sale agreements with Glencore for spodumene concentrate and lithium fines

Final Investment Decision approved for Finniss restart, backed by a ~A$290m funding package: A$120m equity placement (institutional, $0.21/share) plus a US$120m strategic package - US$70m convertible notes (Glencore Australia Holdings and InfraVia) and US$50m senior secured loan (Nebari)
Open-pit mining recommenced at Grants; underground development contract awarded to Develop Global for BP33 (A$274m, 3-year term)

First stockpile shipment (20kt lithium fines + 5kt spodumene concentrate) exported via Darwin Port; divestment of non-core uranium assets to Elevate Uranium; spin-out of NT/SA gold exploration assets into Axiant Resources IPO
First spodumene concentrate produced at the recommissioned Finniss plant, within six months of FID and on schedule; shares rose ~8% on the milestone

September-quarter report: quarter-end cash of ~A$199.7m (up from A$181.8m at 30 June 2026), available funding ~A$244m; Ord Minnett upgraded to Buy (34c target); plant remains in commissioning/optimisation phase ahead of first shipment of new production

FY2026 total stockpile sales of ~A$28.5m (5kt spodumene + 45kt lithium fines), rising to ~A$38.5m including post-year-end sale of remaining 25kt lithium fines; FY2026 cash balance A$182m plus A$103m additional committed funding

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Malcolm McComas and CEO Paul Brown describe FY2026 as transformational, with Finniss repositioned as a lower-cost, de-risked, long-life operation and the company 'fully funded' through BP33 development regardless of short-term lithium market conditions. Management notes continued near-term lithium price volatility but expresses confidence in long-term demand fundamentals (EV adoption, grid storage, electrification) and in Australia's strategic position in critical mineral supply chains.

bull_case: Restart is now de-risked relative to a pure greenfield project: plant, mining fleet and logistics are operational, first concentrate has already been produced (September 2026), and the company reports being fully funded through to BP33 steady-state production
Strategic partners (Glencore, InfraVia, Nebari) provide funding certainty, marketing reach and credibility that a standalone junior miner would lack, reducing financing and offtake risk

Lower-cost restart design (Restart Study: ~40% lower mining costs, ~33% lower processing costs) improves the operation's ability to generate cash flow even if spodumene prices remain well below 2022-2023 peaks
Large, growing Ore Reserve (15.6Mt, up 33-44% at Grants in late 2025) and exploration upside at Blackbeard support a long (~20-year) mine life and optionality beyond current plant capacity

A cyclical recovery in lithium prices (some banks forecasting persistent deficits into 2026-H1 2027) would be highly operationally geared for Core given its fixed cost base and recently expanded production base
bear_case: Core only recently exited a ~2-year suspension of operations caused by a lithium price crash; the restart (ramp-up, plant optimisation, first new shipment, BP33 underground development) is still largely unproven and subject to execution risk

Persistent/deepening global lithium oversupply (per Benchmark Mineral Intelligence and other bearish forecasts) could keep spodumene prices depressed through 2027, squeezing margins just as Core resumes continuous production

The company has never been free-cash-flow positive on a sustained basis and has funded itself through continuous equity dilution (shares outstanding up ~12x since 2016) plus, for the first time, meaningful debt/convertible notes from the FY2026 restart package, adding financial risk and future dilution overhang
Single-asset, sub-scale producer relative to tier-1 peers (Pilbara Minerals, Greenbushes, Mt Marion/Wodgina) with less resilience to another down-cycle

Revenue reported in FY2025/H1 FY2026 was zero or negative (quotation-period price adjustments only, no actual sales), underscoring how binary the investment case is on successful execution of the 2026-2028 restart and ramp-up plan
